subject: FinTechX POC Observability plan & success criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechx.com>, Bob Taylor <bob.taylor@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 21:30:00 +0000
Subject: FinTechX POC Observability plan & success criteria

Hi Alice / Bob —

Thanks again for the call earlier today. As promised, quick recap and a proposed observability plan for the 3-week POC so we can agree success criteria and ownership. High-level goal is to validate latency, throughput, and end-to-end reliability for your customer-facing inference flows while giving your SREs the signals they need to evaluate production readiness.

Recap / Success criteria (proposed):
- Latency: p95 end-to-end latency < 250ms for the targeted demo traffic pattern (50 RPS peak).
- Throughput: sustain 50 req/s with <= 5% queuing at peak.
- Error rate: <0.5% client-visible errors (4xx/5xx while excluding expected model fallback responses).
- Cost proxy: tokens per response and average cost per 1k tokens within the target range we discussed.
- Observability: dashboards + traces + logs available to FinTechX SREs with retention for the POC window and an export option.

Proposed Observability Plan (we'll attach a mock dashboard & runbook):
1) Dashboards (hosted link + PNG attached)
   - Overview: p50/p95/p99 latency, RPS, error rate, request size, response size.
   - Model ops: per-model token usage, cache hit rate, KV cache metrics.
   - Infrastructure: GPU utilization, queue length, host-level CPU/memory, network egress.
   - Business signals: requests by route, top error classes, fallback rate to smaller model.
2) Tracing
   - Correlate client request-id through our SDK -> server -> model runtime spans.
   - Sampling: 10% by default, 100% for error traces; ability to increase sampling during deep-dive windows.
3) Logs & export
   - Structured request logs with request_id, route, model, tokens_in/tokens_out, response_time_ms.
   - Export: S3-compatible export (daily) and an option to forward to your Splunk/CloudWatch/ELK in near-real-time.
4) Alerts / thresholds (examples)
   - p95 latency > 300ms for 5m -> P1 alert.
   - error rate > 1% for 5m -> P1.
   - cache hit rate < 60% -> P2.
5) Ownership & timeline
   - Redwood lead: Marissa Cole (sales/coordination) + Jordan Blake (technical/solutions)
   - FinTechX lead: TBD (please confirm)
   - Kickoff instrumentation: target Mon Apr 26 - instrumentation + access to dashboard mock
   - POC window: Apr 27 - May 14 (3 weeks of validation)

Next steps:
- Can you confirm who will own instrumentation on the FinTechX side?
- We’ll provision dashboard access and share the runbook (attached) before the kickoff.
- If agreed, I’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff with Jordan and Sean to walk through SDK headers, sample logs, and S3 export configuration.

Attachments: poc-observability-dashboard-mock.png, poc-observability-runbook-v1.pdf

Thanks Marissa — this looks sensible and aligned with what we discussed. A few clarification questions before we lock the kickoff:

2) Tracing: the sampling strategy sounds fine. Can you include span names/keys you’ll emit so our tracer team can wire up dashboards on our side?
3) Dashboards: the mock looks great. Will we be able to filter by tenant_id and route? We need that to validate per-customer behavior.

Appreciate it,
Alice

alice.chen@fintechx.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alice Chen <alice.chen@fintechx.com>, Bob Taylor <bob.taylor@fintechx.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 15:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: FinTechX POC Observability plan & success criteria

Thanks Alice — great questions. Answers below and a slightly expanded checklist so we can confirm responsibilities before kickoff. Quoting your questions inline.

> 1) Log export: can you confirm format (JSONL) and whether we can get an incremental export to our S3 bucket (we prefer server-side encryption + lifecycle rules to 90d)?

- Yes: we can export request logs as JSON Lines (JSONL). We support S3 PUT with server-side encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) and can push daily increments (or hourly if needed). Retention inside Redwood for the POC will be 30 days by default; we will configure an export so FinTechX maintains a copy for 90d via your lifecycle rules. We’ll need an S3 write role/ARN from you for initial provisioning.

> 2) Tracing: the sampling strategy sounds fine. Can you include span names/keys you’ll emit so our tracer team can wire up dashboards on our side?

- Yes — we will emit the following span names/keys: request.received, runtime.model_dispatch, runtime.kv_lookup, runtime.model_generate, response.sent. Key fields: request_id, tenant_id, route, model_name, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms. We’ll share a mapping doc in the runbook attachment.

> 3) Dashboards: the mock looks great. Will we be able to filter by tenant_id and route? We need that to validate per-customer behavior.

- Yes — all dashboard panels support filtering by tenant_id and route. We’ll also add a quick selector for time window presets and a pre-built view for the POC success criteria.

Expanded checklist / responsibilities:
- FinTechX (owner: Bob Taylor)
  - Provide S3 write role/ARN for export (by Apr 24)
  - Wire SDK request_id/tenant_id headers into client requests (by Apr 26)
  - Validate sample traces (by Apr 28)
- Redwood (owners: Jordan Blake / Sean Gallagher)
  - Provision dashboard access + attach mock (today)
  - Add tracing keys and sampling policy to the runbook (attached)
  - Configure S3 export to provided ARN and validate write (by Apr 26)

Proposed timeline (short):
- Apr 24: FinTechX provides S3 details + confirmation of owner (Bob)
- Apr 26: Instrumentation completed by both sides; Redwood provisions dashboards and completes S3 write test
- Apr 27: POC kickoff and traffic ramp; begin 3-week validation window

Attachments included: poc-observability-dashboard-mock.png (dashboard screenshot), poc-observability-runbook-v1.pdf (span keys, sample logs, API for export).

If that looks good I’ll send a calendar invite for Apr 27 10:00 PT for the kickoff with Jordan + Sean + Bob.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
